exact_statement: The unqualified assertion that planar iid nonnegative edge-weight FPP has no bi-infinite geodesic is false: for tau_e=1 almost surely, gamma_k=(k,0), k in Z, is a bi-infinite geodesic.
assumptions: all weights equal 1, a degenerate iid law
proof_or_counterexample: Any path from (i,0) to (j,0) has at least |j-i| edges. The horizontal segment has exactly |j-i| edges and cost |j-i|; every finite segment minimizes passage time.
remaining_gap: No gap in this counterexample; it does not refute a statement restricted to continuous weights.

exact_statement: For finite nonnegative nearest-neighbor weights on Z^2, E_n is existence of a simple global geodesic through 0 with endpoints on S_n={||x||_infinity=n} and all other vertices in B_(n-1). These events decrease and their intersection is exactly existence of a bigeodesic through 0. Hence P(H)=lim P(E_n). Under a translation-invariant law, absence everywhere is equivalent to this limit being zero.
assumptions: translation invariance only for the everywhere conclusion

source.prior_context: Survey arXiv:1511.03262 Section 4.5.1 equation (4.25); local at-p0117 anchoring obstruction

proof_or_counterexample: Stop both sides at their first boundary encounter; global geodesic subpaths minimize. At each finite central path length there are finitely many strings. Diagonal infinite-pigeonhole selection yields a simple doubly infinite path, with every segment inherited from a global minimizer. Measurability is finite choice over witnesses and countable comparisons against paths; continuity from above and a countable translated union finish.
remaining_gap: Elementary reduction only; P(E_n)->0 has not been obtained. Review pending and no novelty claim.

exact_statement: Under the continuous iid FPP assumptions A1 of arXiv:2208.11576 (including E[min of four independent weights squared]<infinity), let T_x be the union of all infinite geodesic rays from x and q(z)=P(z in T_0). If H is existence of a bigeodesic through 0, then P(H)<=one-half sum_{x in S_n}q(-x)<=4n sup_{x in S_n}q(x). Vanishing shell sum along a deterministic subsequence, or the stronger sup shell q=o(1/n), implies almost-sure absence everywhere.
assumptions: iid finite nonnegative weights with continuous law
T_x denotes all infinite rays, not a selected family
proof_or_counterexample: Every bigeodesic through 0 supplies two distinct first boundary hits x,y and rays from each through 0; therefore 2*1_H<=sum_{x in S_n}1_{0 in T_x}. Take expectations, translate, and use |S_n|=8n. No multiplication or independence of ray events occurs.
remaining_gap: Published q(z)->0 gives no required shell-sum decay or o(1/n) rate; these are additional unproved premises. Independent review pending.

exact_statement: Vanishing maximal prescribed-witness probability does not imply vanishing probability of existence of some witness, even if the union events are decreasing. For U uniform[0,1), A_(n,j)={floor(n^2 U)=j}, 0<=j<n^2, satisfies max_j P(A_(n,j))=1/n^2 while P(union_j A_(n,j))=1 for every n. In the root-crossing union over S_n endpoint pairs there are 32n^2-4n possibilities.
assumptions: the logical implication is asserted without a union estimate or rate
abstract uniform witness model; not an iid FPP counterexample

proof_or_counterexample: The cells partition[0,1) into n^2 equal intervals. Union events equal the whole sample space. binomial(8n,2)=32n^2-4n; a uniform o(n^-2) pair bound suffices by a union bound but mere convergence to zero does not.
remaining_gap: No gap in the abstract counterexample; it only rejects an inference. Review pending.

exact_statement: If all nearest-neighbor weights obey 0<a<=t_e<=b<infinity, then every global distance between u,v in B_n can be computed inside B_R for R=n+ceil(4bn/a). Consequently E_n uses only edges in B_R. The B_n-restricted metric alone need not identify global minimizing paths.
assumptions: no iid assumption or uniqueness needed

source.measurement: MEASUREMENTS.json: 168 bounded-law finite comparisons and a box-cost 20/global-upper 10 example

proof_or_counterexample: A coordinate path inside B_n costs at most 4bn. Any competitor no dearer has at most floor(4bn/a) edges and stays in B_R. Finitely many such paths exist, so the infimum is attained there. A separate explicit ten-edge detour costing 10 outside B_1 beats the minimizing B_1 path through 0 costing 20.
remaining_gap: Review pending; finite comparisons support code arithmetic only, not an asymptotic probability theorem.

exact_statement: For independent edgewise triples X_e~G,U_e~Uniform[0,1],Z_e~G conditioned on [b,infinity), let a<b, p_a=G([0,a])>0,p_b=G([b,infinity))>0, deterministic 0<=delta_e<p_a on a deterministic finite set F, xi_e=1{X_e<=a,U_e<=delta_e/p_a}, and Y_e=Z_e if xi_e=1 and X_e otherwise. Conditional on the entire individual output Y (unchanged exterior included), the xi_e for e in F are independent Bernoulli variables with parameters 1_[b,infinity)(Y_e) delta_e/(p_b+delta_e). The same kernel restricts to any finite simple path prefix selected from Y alone.
assumptions: no conditioning on another site's output or later marking success

audited_primary.title: No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation

source.measurement: MEASUREMENTS.json: 36 exact posterior products and nine output-measurable selections

proof_or_counterexample: Compute P(xi=1,Y in dt)=delta/p_b*1_high(t)G(dt) and P(xi=0,Y in dt)=[1-delta/p_a*1_low(t)]G(dt). Divide by their positive sum density. Independence of pairs gives the finite output product kernel, and independence of unchanged exterior plus a monotone class argument gives full output conditioning. The selected distinct finite edge list is fixed by that conditioning.
remaining_gap: Independent review pending. This validates only the posterior lemma under exact conditioning, not the bigeodesic theorem or its geometric inputs.
